chapters.title: The map
chapters.summary: The two tracks, the four kinds of code, which directory is which layer, what is built and what is not, and how to read the state tags.

chapters.title: The processor: real mode, protected mode and the A20 gate
chapters.summary: Segments and offsets, the 1 MiB limit and the A20 gate, descriptors and the GDT, the switch to protected mode, interrupts, and what a 486 lacks.

chapters.title: The devices of a 486 PC
chapters.summary: The ISA bus and port I/O, the PICs, the PIT, the 8042, the 16550, VGA and VBE, the floppy, and the BIOS services the project calls.

chapters.title: The boot sector and the loader
chapters.summary: The floppy image, the 512-byte boot sector, stage 2, the A20 test, the memory map, the boot information block, the switch and the copy to 1 MiB.

chapters.title: The boot, end to end
chapters.summary: Power-on to boot complete, one transcript line at a time, the test modes, and how a run ends and what its exit status means.

chapters.title: The kernel: tables, interrupts and the timer
chapters.summary: The kernel's GDT and IDT, remapping the PICs, the IRQ registry, end-of-interrupt, and the PIT at 100 Hz.

chapters.title: The kernel: memory and the x87
chapters.summary: The memory map as the loader leaves it, the frame bitmap, the heap, the usable-RAM arithmetic and the x87 set-up.

chapters.title: The kernel: calling the BIOS from protected mode
chapters.summary: Why the kernel needs the BIOS, the switching sequence, the Bios trait, what was measured, and what V86 would add.

chapters.title: The HAL
chapters.summary: The contract crate: port I/O, memory-mapped regions, interrupts, time, video and input, the mock platform and the host tests.

chapters.title: Drivers I: serial, interrupt controllers and the timer
chapters.summary: The 16550, the two 8259s and the 8254: their register sequences, their tests and how each track uses them.

chapters.title: Drivers II: keyboard and mouse
chapters.summary: The 8042, scancodes, the PS/2 mouse packet, the event contract, the hand-off through rings, and INT 33h on DOS.

chapters.title: Drivers III: VGA and VBE
chapters.summary: Register-programmed modes 13h and 12h, the DAC, text mode, VBE over the Bios trait, the linear frame buffer and the software cursor.

chapters.title: The core I: surfaces, damage and presenting
chapters.summary: The 8-bit back buffer, rectangles and sprites, dirty rectangles, the compositor, frame digests and the presenters.

chapters.title: The core II: text, themes and window chrome
chapters.summary: Reading .DFN files, measuring and drawing text, roles and palettes, the window chrome, icons and the first widgets.

chapters.title: The core III: windows, events and scenarios
chapters.summary: The window manager, Shell::handle and Shell::frame, the cursor, the scenario format and the seam the platforms call.

chapters.title: Two platforms, one core
chapters.summary: What a platform is, the native shell mode and SHELL.EXE side by side, and why there is no Platform trait yet.

chapters.title: The hosted runtime and the build to SHELL.EXE
chapters.summary: DOS extenders and DPMI, the runtime contract, the heap, INT 21h, the IRQ stubs, and the build from Rust to an executable.

chapters.title: Fonts and formats
chapters.summary: The bitmap faces, .DFN byte by byte, one source for three formats, the outline faces, the emoji and the formats still planned.

chapters.title: The toolchain and the custom targets
chapters.summary: The pinned toolchain, the three target files compared, build-std, the linker, elf2bin and the Docker images.

chapters.title: The machines we run on
chapters.summary: QEMU as a 486, Bochs, 86Box, DOSBox Staging and js-dos, how each run is driven, and the standing caveat about real hardware.

chapters.title: Testing and the evidence method
chapters.summary: Nothing is promoted without evidence: host tests, expected transcripts, negative checks, golden frames, CI and the three shelves.

chapters.title: What is not built
chapters.summary: Every planned box said plainly: apps, the SDK, system calls, a loader, processes, paging, storage, sound and FreeDOS.
